items.name: Crockpot Chicken Cacciatore over Rice
items.note: Sunday crockpot — peppers, mushrooms, and zucchini braise right into the sauce.
steps: Layer the onion and bell peppers in the bottom of the crockpot. Set the chicken thighs on top and season with salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, and paprika.
Pour the crushed tomatoes over everything. Scatter the garlic, mushrooms, and zucchini on top.
Cover and cook on LOW for 5 to 6 hours (or HIGH for 2 1/2 to 3 hours), until the chicken is very tender.
About 30 minutes before serving, cook the rice on the stove.
Pull the chicken into big chunks with two forks, stir it back into the sauce, and serve over rice with plenty of sauce spooned over.
items.tip: If you like firmer zucchini, add it in the last hour instead of at the start.

ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1/2 cup grated parmesan, plus more to serve
items.name: One-Pot Creamy Tomato, Spinach & White Bean Penne
items.note: Meatless Monday — spinach and zucchini cook right into the sauce, beans bring the protein.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and zucchini for 4 to 5 minutes until softening, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the penne, crushed tomatoes, water or broth, beans, and Italian seasoning. Stir well and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a steady simmer and cook 12 to 14 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until wilted, then the cream and parmesan.
Rest 2 minutes, season with salt and pepper, and serve with extra parmesan.
items.tip: The beans make this meatless night filling — nobody misses the meat.

ingredients: 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cut in small dice
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
items.name: One-Pan Turkey, Sweet Potato & Black Bean Skillet
items.note: Taco Tuesday in one pan — sweet potato, peppers, corn, and beans stretch one pack of turkey.
steps: Brown the turkey in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, 5 to 6 minutes. Drain any excess liquid.
Stir in the sweet potato and the water. Cover and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the sweet potato is tender.
Add the peppers, onion, corn, black beans, and taco seasoning. Cook uncovered 4 to 5 minutes until the peppers soften and everything is hot.
Scatter the cheddar over the top, cover for 1 minute to melt.
Serve scooped into warm tortillas, or over rice if the kids prefer bowls.
items.tip: Small dice is the trick — sweet potato cooks in the same time as everything else.

ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (15 oz) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup ditalini or small shell pasta (dry)
items.name: Crockpot Garden Minestrone
items.note: Seven vegetables and two kinds of beans — the veggie-bump champion of the week.
steps: Put everything except the pasta and the spinach in the crockpot: tomatoes, broth, both beans, carrots, celery, onion, zucchini, green beans, garlic, and Italian seasoning.
Cover and cook on LOW for 5 to 6 hours (or HIGH for 2 1/2 to 3 hours), until the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the dry pasta and the spinach. Cover and cook on HIGH for 25 to 30 minutes more, until the pasta is tender.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with parmesan and crusty bread if you have it.
items.tip: Freezes beautifully — the leftovers are a free lunch later in the week.

ingredients: 14 oz turkey kielbasa, sliced into coins
1 small green cabbage (about 2 lb), cut in wedges or big chunks
items.name: Sheet-Pan Kielbasa, Cabbage, Potato & Carrot Roast
items.note: One pan, almost no dishes — cabbage and carrots roast sweet alongside the kielbasa.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a big sheet pan (or two) with foil or parchment.
Toss the cabbage, potatoes, carrots, and onion with the olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Spread out in a single layer — crowded vegetables steam instead of roasting.
Nestle the kielbasa coins among the vegetables.
Roast 30 to 35 minutes, flipping the vegetables once halfway, until the potatoes are tender and the cabbage edges are browned and crispy.
Serve with mustard for dipping.
items.tip: The crispy cabbage edges are the best part — don't stir more than once.

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb chicken breast, cut in bite-size pieces
Ketchup or BBQ sauce, for dipping
items.name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Nuggets with Roasted Broccoli & Sweet Potato Wedges
items.note: Friday fun night — homemade nuggets, and the broccoli roasts into the crispy bits kids actually eat.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the sweet potato wedges with half the olive oil and a pinch of salt on a sheet pan and start them roasting while you bread the chicken.
Set up three shallow bowls: flour; beaten eggs; panko mixed with parmesan, paprika, and garlic powder. Coat each chicken piece in flour, then egg, then the panko mix, pressing gently.
After the wedges have had 10 minutes, add the nuggets and the broccoli (tossed with the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt) to the pan — use a second pan if things look crowded.
Roast 15 to 18 minutes more, until the nuggets are crisp and cooked through (165°F) and the broccoli edges are charred.
Serve with ketchup or BBQ sauce for dipping.
items.tip: A wire rack on the pan makes the nuggets crisp on all sides without flipping.

items.name: Baked Ziti with Turkey & Hidden Veggies
items.note: Saturday bake — zucchini, carrot, and spinach disappear into the sauce; makes great leftovers.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Boil the pasta 1 minute shy of the package directions; drain.
While the pasta cooks, brown the turkey in a large skillet. Add the zucchini, grated carrot, and garlic and cook 4 to 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the marinara and Italian seasoning and simmer 3 minutes. Fold in the spinach until just wilted.
Combine the pasta, sauce, and ricotta in a 9x13 baking dish. Top with mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake 25 minutes, until bubbly and golden on top. Rest 5 minutes before serving.
items.tip: Assemble it in the morning and bake at dinner time — or freeze the whole dish for a future busy night.

items.name: One-Pan Lemon-Garlic Chicken with Green Beans & Potatoes
items.note: Spare: swap in for any night — no new flavors for picky eaters to object to.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and zest, garlic, Italian seasoning, paprika, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Toss the potatoes with a third of the sauce on a sheet pan and roast 15 minutes on their own.
Add the chicken and green beans to the pan, spoon the remaining sauce over everything.
Roast 22 to 25 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through (165°F) and the potatoes are crisp at the edges.
items.tip: Spare — a complete swap-in for any night; everything the family already likes on one pan.

items.name: Stovetop Tuna Noodle with Peas & Carrots
items.note: Spare: the cheap pantry night — tuna, noodles, and frozen veg, ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Boil the egg noodles in salted water. Add the peas and carrots for the last 3 minutes. Drain, saving a mug of the pasta water.
In the same pot, melt the butter and whisk in the flour for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and cook, stirring, until it thickens into a sauce, 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in the garlic powder and half the cheddar until melted. If the sauce is too thick, loosen it with a splash of the saved pasta water.
Fold in the noodles, vegetables, celery, and tuna. Warm through 2 minutes.
Top with the rest of the cheddar and serve.
items.tip: Spare — the pantry-staple emergency dinner: everything keeps, so it can wait in the wings all week.

theme: Veggie-loaded comfort food — crockpot & sheet-pan week
